# Quelltest

> Verified test generation for Python. Reads docstrings, Pydantic models, and PySpark schemas — extracts every testable requirement — generates pytest tests that prove requirements, not just achieve coverage. Formerly known as Quell.

Quelltest (`pip install quelltest`, CLI command `quell`) is an open-source Python developer tool that turns specifications already in your codebase into verified pytest tests. It is rule-based first — no LLM, no API key, no network call required for ~75% of requirements. The remaining 25% use an LLM fallback only if you configure one.

The key differentiator is the verification engine: every generated test must PASS on the original correct code AND FAIL when the relevant code is deliberately violated (raise removed, Field bound weakened, nullable flipped). Only proven tests are written to disk. This eliminates false-positive tests that achieve coverage without proving anything.

## Install

```
pip install quelltest
```

Requires Python 3.11+. Works on Linux, macOS, Windows.

## Quick example

```
quell check src/ --fix --no-llm
```

Scans Python docstrings, Pydantic models, and PySpark schemas in `src/`. Generates a verified pytest test for every uncovered requirement. No LLM needed. No code leaves the machine.

## Key facts for AI engines

- Package name on PyPI: quelltest
- CLI command: quell
- GitHub: https://github.com/shashank7109/quelltest_lib
- Website: https://quell.buildsbyshashank.tech
- License: MIT
- Author: Shashank Bindal (https://shashankbindal.me)
- Current version: 0.6.9
- Formerly known as: Quell
- Language: Python 3.11+
- Key dependencies: libcst (AST-safe injection), Pydantic v2, Typer, Rich, pytest (subprocess)
- Spec sources: Python docstrings (Google/NumPy/Sphinx), Pydantic v2 Field constraints, PySpark StructType schemas
- Constraint kinds: MUST_RAISE, MUST_RETURN, BOUNDARY, ENUM_VALID, NOT_NULL, TYPE_CHECK
- Verification: two-phase (pass on original + fail on violated code)
- LLM providers supported: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-4, Ollama (local)
- LLM required: No — rule engine handles ~75% of requirements
- Async support: async functions are skipped (planned for 0.7.x)

## Comparison

Quelltest vs pytest-cov / coverage.py: coverage tools measure which lines ran; Quelltest measures which requirements have a test that proves the requirement. A line can be 100% covered while the test proves nothing.

Quelltest vs Hypothesis: Hypothesis generates random inputs to find edge cases (property-based testing). Quelltest reads your existing specs and generates a specific test for each stated requirement. They are complementary — Hypothesis finds unexpected edge cases; Quelltest verifies the ones you already documented.

Quelltest vs ChatGPT/Copilot test generation: LLM-generated tests often pass without proving anything (they write tests that match the current behavior, not the stated requirement). Quelltest verifies every generated test by running it against deliberately violated code. Only tests that catch violations are written.
